title: Event-sourced ledger for reserved throughput drift detection and retroactive SLA credits
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: customers on Dedicated pools expect predictable reserved throughput. Recent incidents showed divergence between observed throughput and what the billing system recorded when transient node/driver restarts and clock skew occurred. Root cause: non-deterministic aggregation windows, out-of-order usage events, and silent drops of intermediate burst tokens. Goal: implement an event-sourced usage ledger plus a fingerprinting reconciliation pass that produces deterministic, auditable adjustments (retroactive SLA credits and corrected billing lines) while keeping tail latency and write throughput for the runtime low. The ledger must support idempotent ingestion from runtime components, detect duplicate or missing batches, and produce compact audit exports for finance and customer-visible usage history.
acceptance_criteria: An append-only event ledger ingest API exists and is consumed by dedicated runtime agents for all pool-level meter events (reserved allocations, burst grants, token burns, backfills)
Ledger entries are idempotent by (pool_id,event_seq,event_hash) and survive service restarts without duplication
Reconciliation job can compute per-tenant effective reserved throughput over arbitrary historical windows and produce SLA credit values matching test oracle for five representative incidents
Retroactive crediting pipeline emits adjustment records to billing ledger and exposes human-readable audit records in NDJSON for the last 90 days
End-to-end latency impact on request path is <1ms p95 for the runtime agent RPC used to emit meter events
New dashboard shows fingerprint diffs and a reconciliation score; false-positive rate <1% over synthetic test traffic
Automated tests cover out-of-order event ingestion, clock skew >5s, partial window reprocessing, and double-emit recovery
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for ledger ingestion and idempotence. 2) Integration in staging with injected out-of-order and duplicate events using the runtime fault injector. 3) Four synthetic incident replays (node flaps, slow driver, clock skew, partial network partition) with an oracle script that computes expected credits. 4) End-to-end smoke before deploy: create dedicated pool, exercise bursts, intentionally drop events and validate reconciliation output. 5) Canary release to <10% of pools for 48 hours, monitor reconciliation-score and billing-adjustment rate.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy ledger write API and staging ingestion consumers. Phase 2: Enable fingerprinting offline worker and generate reconciliation reports (read-only). Phase 3: Wire billing adjustments behind feature flag and run canary pools. Phase 4: Gradual ramp to all new Dedicated pools and backfill historical 90-day window in batch mode.
decisions: Use append-only event store (WAL-backed) in billing namespace instead of immediate relational writes to allow replay and deterministic reprocessing
Fingerprinting will use a deterministic hash over windowed token grants + TTL-sorted event_seq rather than sequence numbers alone to handle agent restarts
Retro credit calculation will be amortized over the billing period to avoid one-off large refunds affecting invoices
tradeoffs: Storing full events for 90 days increases storage costs but dramatically simplifies audits and customer support investigations
Strong idempotence and dedupe requires additional metadata emissions from runtime agents (small increase in RPC payloads) but avoids costly manual reconciliations
Real-time correction vs batch: real-time adjustments reduce customer-visible lag but increase operational blast radius; we choose conservative batch adjustments with canary gating

2026-01-14 Reliability review: flagged clock skew scenarios where agent heartbeat >10s leads to duplicated grants. Added fingerprinting to decisions.

notes_for_support: Support runbook: if customer disputes usage, run ledger fingerprint diff tool for the pool_id and provide NDJSON export; flag for manual review if reconciliation score <0.95
observability_requirements: Expose reconciliation_score, event_ingest_latency_ms_p95, duplicate_event_rate, credit_adjustment_rate as alerts with 1h burn-in
migration_strategy: Backfill last 90 days using batched replay from raw runtime logs into event ledger; run reconciliation in read-only mode and compare with current billing. If delta <0.01% apply automated amortized credits; otherwise escalate for manual review.
